nodes.label: Port mode vs network mode container orchestration
nodes.rationale: Network mode (FRC_CONTAINER_NETWORK set) joins containers to a shared Docker network with no published ports, using container-name endpoints instead of host ports; FRC_HOST_DATA_DIR translates bind-mount paths for a differently-rooted host mount; matches AGENTS.md decision 031.

nodes.label: Container adoption safety checks
nodes.rationale: ensureCodeContainer refuses to adopt a running container with non-loopback port bindings, mismatched frc-sim labels, or a bind-mounted /config when demo mode expects a volume — it removes and recreates instead, but restarts (not recreates) a stopped container with correct labels/ports.

nodes.label: Superseded run must not clobber newer run's status
nodes.rationale: When run B supersedes run A on the same workspace, A's deferred terminal finishJob (exiting later) must not overwrite the shared workspace snapshot once it belongs to B — guarded by run-id identity check.

nodes.label: Startup marks persisted active runs as stopped
nodes.rationale: On control-plane restart, any run job persisted as running/building is orphaned (its process is gone) and gets marked stopped with finished_at set, so /api/sim/status reflects reality after a crash/restart.
nodes.norm_label: startup marks persisted active runs as stopped

nodes.label: Container self-inspection auto-detection
nodes.rationale: selfInspect derives hostDataDir, containerNetwork, and containerUser by docker-inspecting the control container's own bind mounts/networks/uid so FRC_HOST_DATA_DIR/FRC_CONTAINER_NETWORK/FRC_CONTAINER_USER are optional overrides; refuses to derive a root uid/gid, and hard-errors (never silently falls back to port mode) when detection is ambiguous — matches decision 031.

nodes.label: Auto-chooser NT4 bridge msgpack decoding
nodes.rationale: The auto-chooser API bridges to NT4 binary msgpack frames to discover SmartDashboard chooser topics, must ignore malformed frames without crashing, and republishes the selected topic after an NT4 reconnect.

nodes.label: TOCTOU symlink race guard (deploy files)
nodes.rationale: Path-based checks (lstat/realpath on directory components) are check-then-use and can lose a race against a directory swapped for a symlink between check and open. Opening the file first and then resolving the already-open descriptor via /proc/self/fd closes that race because the descriptor names the inode actually opened and cannot be re-pointed. O_NOFOLLOW blocks a symlink as the final path segment. Falls back to path-only checks (fail-open) on hosts without /proc/self/fd (e.g. macOS) since deployments run on Linux.

nodes.label: Single WS upgrade entry point pattern
nodes.rationale: All server.upgrade( calls in this file are funneled through upgradeWebSocket() which bakes in the origin/CSRF check, so a new WS route added later cannot silently skip that check; reviewers are told to reject any server.upgrade( call outside this helper.
nodes.norm_label: single ws upgrade entry point pattern

nodes.label: Reload allowlist before each sign-in check
nodes.rationale: Reloading allowlist.json from disk before enforcing it lets CLI edits (coderunner allowlist add) take effect on the next sign-in attempt without an admin-panel reload or restart. A stale cache is acceptable on reload failure (fallback), but a hard sign-in crash is not.
nodes.norm_label: reload allowlist before each sign-in check

nodes.label: Default-deny session gating pattern
nodes.rationale: Centralized helpers (requireSession, requireWorkspaceOwnership, requireAdmin) replace old per-route authFromRequest + resolveWorkspaceRequest checks, ensuring every non-public route defaults to denying access unless explicitly gated.

nodes.label: Two-source lesson catalog pattern (bundled + remote)
nodes.rationale: BundledCatalogSource reads modules.json baked into the code image at /opt/frc-catalog for zero-config/offline demos; RemoteCatalogSource fetches modules.json from a configured GitHub repo/branch with a 60s cache and falls back to last-good cache on fetch failure. createCatalogSource picks remote when LESSONS_CATALOG_REPO is configured, else bundled.

nodes.label: Reject root workspace-container user in network mode
nodes.rationale: Inside a container the control-plane process usually runs as root, so mirroring 'my own uid:gid' would silently run workspace containers as root and root-own student files on the host data disk. Network mode (FRC_CONTAINER_NETWORK set) is the marker for a containerized deployment, so loadControlConfig throws at boot if containerUser resolves to uid 0 without an explicit override (FRC_CONTAINER_USER or FRC_UID/FRC_GID).
nodes.norm_label: reject root workspace-container user in network mode

nodes.label: Characterization-test-before-refactor pattern
nodes.rationale: Tests pin createWebSocketHandlers' current open/message/close behavior across socket kinds (plan 008) so a later shared-bridge refactor (plan 009) has a fast regression net; they assert existing behavior and make no production changes, deliberately leaving the real-upstream WebSocket open path to the e2e tier.

nodes.label: entry.socket !== socket stale-guard pattern
nodes.rationale: Every listener's first line checks entry.socket !== socket so a late callback from a superseded socket can never mutate the live entry — first line of defense against stale WebSocket callbacks.

nodes.label: Decision 018 (gamepad unplug safety)
nodes.rationale: Anchors a regression test ensuring unplugging the selected gamepad clears frame and selection state, tied to commit cb9fea6.

nodes.label: Import/Lesson-load Shared Streaming Protocol
nodes.rationale: Both GitHub import (ws/import) and lesson load (ws/lesson-load) speak the exact same importServerMessage streaming protocol, so they share one hook and one progress UI instead of duplicating logic.

nodes.label: Cloudflare 100s Idle Timeout Keepalive Ping
nodes.rationale: A 30s ping interval keeps the run WebSocket alive through Cloudflare's 100-second idle timeout when connected and idle.

nodes.label: Exponential Backoff Reconnect
nodes.rationale: On socket close, reconnect delay doubles from 500ms up to a 10s cap before retrying the connection.

nodes.label: AdvantageScope Iframe postMessage Handshake
nodes.rationale: Configures the embedded AdvantageScope Lite iframe with the NT4 websocket/alive endpoints via postMessage, waiting up to 10s for an ack before falling back to a timeout state.

nodes.label: Workspace Activity Heartbeat
nodes.rationale: Sends a heartbeat every 60s (and on pagehide with closing=true) so the control plane can account for idle containers and reclaim them.

nodes.label: reloadKey Manual Refetch Trigger
nodes.rationale: reloadKey is bumped after a project swap to force a session refetch so currentModule/currentModuleKind/projectEmpty stay in sync.

nodes.label: 1s Poll + Visibility-triggered Refresh
nodes.rationale: Polls sim status every 1s and also refreshes immediately when the document becomes visible again, to keep DS/robot status current.

nodes.label: WPILib XboxController Axis/Button Layout
nodes.rationale: Maps the browser Gamepad API's standard mapping to the WPILib XboxController axis/button layout that HALSim consumes, per the W3C Gamepad remapping spec.

nodes.label: Keyboard-as-Virtual-Gamepad Emulation
nodes.rationale: Keyboard input is mapped to the same GamepadState shape used by real gamepads (WASD/arrows/QOEU/etc.) so students without a physical controller can still drive the sim, and the visualizer can render keyboard input identically to a real gamepad via gamepadStateToVisualizerFrame.

nodes.label: Roster-based Access Gating
nodes.rationale: A 'forbidden' or roster-related auth error is surfaced with a friendly message telling the student to ask their coach to add them to the roster, reflecting that sign-in is gated by coach-managed roster membership rather than open registration.

nodes.label: plain-java Console Lesson Gating
nodes.rationale: plain-java console lessons hide the sim chrome and pass a null slug to sim data hooks (useRunChannel, useSimulationState, useAutoChoosers, useScopeHandshake) so they no-op and stop idle HALSim/run sockets and polls, saving resources for lessons that don't need robot simulation.

nodes.label: First-login Auto-open Switch Project (D7)
nodes.rationale: An empty workspace auto-opens the Switch Project dialog once so the student starts by picking a lesson, since first-login template seeding was removed.

nodes.label: persist middleware with partialize (inputMode only)
nodes.rationale: Only inputMode is persisted to localStorage under key frc-coderunner-ui; consoleCollapsed/scopeCollapsed are ephemeral per-session UI state and deliberately excluded via partialize.

nodes.label: Vite dev-server proxy rules to control plane
nodes.rationale: Dev server proxies /api, /healthz, /metrics, /scope, /pathplanner, admin routes, and /u/<slug>/* routes to the control plane at localhost:4000 including websocket upgrade, mirroring the production reverse-proxy path shape.
nodes.norm_label: vite dev-server proxy rules to control plane

nodes.label: robot-starter headless sim configuration (no GUI/DS extensions)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately omits wpi.sim.addGui() and wpi.sim.addDriverstation() since the container has no display; enables the HALSim WebSocket server instead so the web Driver Station UI can control enable/disable, mode, and e-stop over the network. See docs/decisions/015 and docs/archive/mvp-docs/decisions/001-sim-container.md.
nodes.norm_label: robot-starter headless sim configuration (no gui/ds extensions)

nodes.label: coderunner-workspace bind-mount contract
nodes.rationale: data/users/<workspaceId>/project mounts to /workspace/project (authoritative student code) and data/users/<workspaceId>/home mounts to /config (Gradle cache, editor state, extensions); ports 3000/3300/5810 published loopback-only since the control plane proxy is the sole browser-facing endpoint.

nodes.label: coderunner-workspace conservative JVM/Gradle memory bounds
nodes.rationale: For classroom density: JDT LS defaults to -Xmx512m (vs WPILib-generated -Xmx8G); Gradle runs bounded via /config/.gradle/gradle.properties (-Xmx384m, no daemon, no VFS watching, two workers) deliberately not duplicated into java.import.gradle.* settings which reject them (decision 037); simulation JVM capped at -Xmx256m unless ROBOT_SIM_JVMARGS overrides.

nodes.label: sim-headless.init.gradle headless HALSim rewiring
nodes.rationale: Removes halsim_gui and halsim_ds_socket dependencies (no X11/display in container), ensures halsim_ws_server is present for remote web Driver Station control, and bounds the robot sim JVM heap (default -Xms32m -Xmx256m ...) so a student program cannot consume the entire per-workspace container budget. Applied via --init-script in start-sim.sh. See docs/decisions/016-imported-project-sim-compat.md.

nodes.label: run-sim.sh two-phase gradle-build-then-exec design
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 runs ./gradlew simulateExternalJava to build, extract JNI natives, and write build/sim/java.json, then exits; Phase 2 parses the descriptor and execs java -jar so the same PID becomes the robot JVM and Gradle is no longer resident in memory during simulation. See decision 025.

nodes.label: render-env.sh fail-closed secret fetch design
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes soft 'no version added yet' (NOT_FOUND) from hard errors (auth/IAM/network): hard errors propagate immediately, while missing-secret detection is deferred to a single validation step so the existing .env is never overwritten on a transient gcloud blip.

nodes.label: Alloy log pipeline bounded active-series design
nodes.rationale: discovery.docker + relabel keeps only the compose 'control' service and copies its service name into a 'unit' label; only level/category are extracted from the JSON body as Loki labels, everything else (workspaceId, runId, durationMs, ...) stays in the body and is queried via `| json` at query time to keep active series bounded.
nodes.norm_label: alloy log pipeline bounded active-series design

nodes.label: Machine settings.json theme seeding
nodes.rationale: OpenVSCode 1.109.5 falls back to light theme if given the display label 'Dark Modern' instead of the id 'Default Dark Modern'; init-frc-setup seeds this key only when absent so User/Workspace settings can still override via normal precedence.

nodes.label: Decision 027: Ship control-plane logs to Grafana Cloud Loki
nodes.norm_label: decision 027: ship control-plane logs to grafana cloud loki

nodes.label: Loki log shipping pipeline
nodes.rationale: Metrics (decision 023) show 'what' is slow but not 'why'; journald+SSH is too slow for classroom incident response. Loki reuses the free Grafana Cloud tier (50GB/14d). JSON NDJSON sink gated by LOG_FORMAT=json keeps bounded labels (job, unit, host, level, category) while high-cardinality fields (workspaceId, runId) stay in the JSON body queried via LogQL `| json`, keeping active streams low. App stays vendor-neutral, same principle as metrics decision 023.

nodes.label: Decision 028: Demo mode for zero-config local tryout
nodes.norm_label: decision 028: demo mode for zero-config local tryout

nodes.label: Synthetic session (demo mode)
nodes.rationale: A single --demo flag seeds one admin user and short-circuits getSessionFromRequest to return a canned session, avoiding a DB write per visitor and a race between cookie minting and the request needing the session; Better Auth's internal flow stays untouched since auth.api.getSession is never called in demo mode. Not safe for public deployment — every visitor resolves to the same admin user.

nodes.label: Bundled vs remote lesson catalog
nodes.rationale: First-login template seeding removed in favor of a lesson catalog picker with two sources (bundled catalog/ baked into image, remote repo via LESSONS_CATALOG_REPO) behind one interface, so production lessons can be edited without an image rebuild while demos/dev/offline stay zero-config.

nodes.label: Backup/restore flow removal
nodes.rationale: Pure discard + git is the safety model for team work rather than server-side per-import backups; backupProject, pruneImportBackups, restoreImportBackup and related routes/UI removed. Operator-level scripts/backup.ts and scripts/restore.ts (full data-dir backup) are retained as unrelated tools.

nodes.label: Stale run-job status write fix
nodes.rationale: finishJob guarded jobsByWorkspace.delete with an id check but not rememberStatus, letting a draining old job overwrite a new run's live status; fix extends the guard to the status write.

nodes.label: Capacity admission on container adoption
nodes.rationale: MAX_ACTIVE_CONTAINERS was enforced only on create, not on adoptCodeContainer's docker start restart path, so a wave of reconnects after an idle sweep could exceed the cap; restart-from-stopped now goes through the same admission control.

nodes.label: Batched docker inspect
nodes.rationale: managedContainerStats issued one docker inspect subprocess per container serially (30-50 spawns per 15s tick); docker container inspect accepts multiple names returning a JSON array, collapsing the fan-out into one subprocess.

nodes.label: Baseline response security headers
nodes.rationale: No baseline security headers were set; X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy now applied at the single response chokepoint guarded by headers.has() so they don't clobber proxied editor/AS Lite headers. Full CSP deliberately deferred since editor and AS Lite rely on inline scripts/eval.

nodes.label: ReconnectingWsBridge base class
nodes.rationale: HalSimBridge and Nt4AutoChooserBridge independently reimplemented the same connection-lifecycle scaffolding and had drifted (halsim grew backoff reconnect nt4 lacked); scaffolding moved into a shared base with hooks (createEntry, createSocket, onSocketOpen, onSocketMessage, onSocketClosed, onSocketError), keeping reconnect strategy itself as an overridable hook.

nodes.label: containers/control/Dockerfile multi-stage build
nodes.rationale: Collapses deploy to 'pull the newest image' and moves the emsdk/AdvantageScope wasm compile inside docker build, so neither CI runners nor operators install emsdk. Runtime stage installs deps with full workspace source present (not manifests-only) because Bun's isolated linker needs the workspace symlinks created during install, discovered after a boot failure ('Cannot find module @logtape/logtape').

nodes.label: Dual-mode runtime provider (port mode / network mode)
nodes.rationale: Port mode (host loopback ports) works for the host dev loop; network mode (FRC_CONTAINER_NETWORK set) joins a shared Docker bridge network with no published host ports since publishing ports doesn't work cleanly from inside a container, proxying via Docker's embedded DNS instead.
nodes.norm_label: dual-mode runtime provider (port mode / network mode)

nodes.label: self-inspect.ts (zero-config containerized mode)
nodes.rationale: FRC_HOST_DATA_DIR, FRC_CONTAINER_NETWORK, FRC_CONTAINER_USER were required env plumbing the control plane can determine itself via docker inspect on its own container; env always wins, inspection only fills gaps, and activation is /.dockerenv-gated with no fallback to port mode (silent fallback would boot a deployment unreachable via published ports).

nodes.label: coderunner dispatching CLI
nodes.rationale: Replaces exposing script filenames (docker compose exec control bun scripts/<name>.ts) as the operator interface with a single entrypoint.sh installed at /usr/local/bin/coderunner dispatching by subcommand.

nodes.label: CODERUNNER_ADMIN_EMAIL bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Collapses two manual exec steps (allowlist then promote) to zero by seeding bootstrap admins at startup and setting role:admin at signup via user.create.before hook.

nodes.label: Non-root control container (USER bun)
nodes.rationale: Control container originally ran as root, writing root:root files to bind-mounted ./data and making an RCE container-escape-trivial. Image now defaults to USER bun (uid 1000); compose overrides identity via CODERUNNER_UID/GID plus CODERUNNER_DOCKER_GID as a supplementary group for socket access. Narrows blast radius but does not eliminate the Docker-socket escape surface.

nodes.label: Canonical registry-qualified image names
nodes.rationale: Build/pull scripts, docker compose, and control plane's CODE_IMAGE default disagreed on bare vs GHCR-qualified image names, causing local rebuilds to be invisible to compose. One canonical name per image (${CODERUNNER_IMAGE_NS}/coderunner-<x>:${CODERUNNER_TAG}) used everywhere; bare names and the pull-side re-tag are deleted; CODERUNNER_IMAGE_NS is the single fork knob.

nodes.label: CODE_DISK_READ_LIMIT (--device-read-bps cap)
nodes.rationale: A cgroup pinned at its memory limit with mostly-reclaimable file-cache pages does not OOM; the kernel evicts and re-faults pages indefinitely, saturating shared Hyperdisk throughput and freezing the whole VM (SSH included). Docker's --device-read-bps throttles a thrashing container's own reads (writes untouched) so it degrades itself instead of the host. Auto-detected from /sys/block only when the control plane itself runs containerized (mirrors decision 031's self-inspection pattern); host/dev runs apply no limit.

nodes.label: CODE_MEMORY_LIMIT raised to 4096m
nodes.rationale: The 2560m/3200m limit that triggered the incident was simply smaller than a cold Gradle build + Java LS + openvscode-server workload (~4GB); the read cap bounds blast radius when a workload still exceeds its limit.

nodes.label: Decision 034: Demo mode portability on Docker Desktop
nodes.norm_label: decision 034: demo mode portability on docker desktop

nodes.label: group_add default CODERUNNER_DOCKER_GID=0
nodes.rationale: Docker Desktop's WSL2 VM owns the socket as root:root, so the Linux-docker-group default never matched and every start died in selfInspect naming unfixable FRC_* variables. Defaulting the single group_add entry to 0 makes Docker Desktop zero-config; Linux hosts must set the real gid. An audit found gid 0 grants access to only three lock files, no real risk given the process already holds the root-equivalent Docker socket.

nodes.label: /config as named volume in demo mode
nodes.rationale: Windows bind mounts served over 9p across the Docker Desktop VM boundary cost ~20ms per file op; seeding thousands of Gradle-cache/extension files this way made first boot 14x slower and the editor readiness probe time out. A named volume lives on the VM's own filesystem, decoupling demo performance from host OS; project/ stays a bind mount since it's the student's actual code.
nodes.norm_label: /config as named volume in demo mode

nodes.label: Decision 035: Multi-Arch Images and CI/Release/Deploy Workflow Split
nodes.norm_label: decision 035: multi-arch images and ci/release/deploy workflow split

nodes.label: ci.yml / release.yml / deploy.yml split
nodes.rationale: Previously everything (verify, image publish, GCE/Cloudflare deploy) lived in one workflow_dispatch pipeline, so tests only ran at deploy time and publishing arm64 images for the community meant touching prod. Splitting lets CI gate every PR/push, release.yml publish multi-arch images on tag push, and deploy.yml only consume a published, verified release.

nodes.label: Multi-arch build via native runners + digest merge
nodes.rationale: A full Gradle/JVM build in a RUN layer rules out QEMU-emulated multi-arch builds (10-20x slower, JIT flakiness); each arch builds on its own native GitHub runner and pushes by digest, then docker buildx imagetools create stitches digests into one manifest list per tag.
nodes.norm_label: multi-arch build via native runners + digest merge

nodes.label: ascope-dist filesystem-only stage reused across arch
nodes.rationale: emscripten/emsdk:4.0.12 publishes no arm64 image, but the AdvantageScope wasm/JS output is architecture-independent, so the arm64 build substitutes a pre-built ascope-dist stage harvested from the amd64 job instead of running emsdk again.
nodes.norm_label: ascope-dist filesystem-only stage reused across arch

nodes.label: Decision 036: Editor migration openvscode-server to VSCodium reh-web
nodes.norm_label: decision 036: editor migration openvscode-server to vscodium reh-web

nodes.label: VSCodium reh-web chosen over code-server
nodes.rationale: openvscode-server stopped releasing (last 1.109.5 vs upstream 1.134.0) and LinuxServer deprecated their openvscode-server image. code-server is better-maintained but lacks --server-base-path (only supports a built-in /absproxy/<port> proxy and infers its base client-side via relative URLs), which would invert the control plane's 'server owns the prefix' proxy contract and make correctness depend permanently on trailing-slash URLs. codium-server supports --server-base-path, verified to emit absolute prefixed asset URLs and honor WebSocket upgrade/?folder= under the prefix unchanged.

nodes.label: linuxserver/vscodium-web base image
nodes.rationale: Built FROM the same baseimage-ubuntu:noble already used, preserving s6-overlay supervision, abc user, PUID/PGID, lsiown, /config as HOME; documented fallback is installing the reh-web tarball directly onto baseimage-ubuntu if LinuxServer deprecates vscodium-web.

nodes.label: --user-data-dir ignored by codium-server (post-review correction)
nodes.rationale: Stock VS Code server unconditionally overwrites the parsed --user-data-dir flag with join(REMOTE_DATA_FOLDER,'data'); openvscode-server only honored it because Gitpod patched that exact line, and VSCodium applies no such patch. Real data root was /config/.vscodium-server/data/, so every setting init-frc-setup seeds was silently unread. Fixed by passing --server-data-dir instead, which derives /config/data/{User,Machine} matching the existing layout.

nodes.label: Workspace trust Restricted Mode issue
nodes.rationale: Fresh workbenches open in Restricted Mode holding redhat.java in Lightweight Mode; security.workspace.trust.enabled is application-scoped and not read from server-side settings.json (same scoping rule that greys the setting out in Remote-SSH). Confirmed pre-existing in the outgoing openvscode-server image too, not a migration regression. Closed by decision 037's --disable-workspace-trust flag.

nodes.label: Webview CDN revision mismatch (post-acceptance correction)
nodes.rationale: linuxserver/vscodium-web:1.126.04524-ls35 shipped webviewContentExternalBaseUrlTemplate pointing at a stale VS Code revision using the older ArrayBuffer webview protocol while the 1.126 workbench used the newer transferable ReadableStream protocol, so no vscode-resource asset (e.g. WPILib Vendor Dependencies webview) could load. Fixed by replacing all eight product.json/out/ occurrences with the correct revision, with a build-time count assertion to catch future drift.

nodes.label: Decision 037: Workspace cache aliases, extension pins, and trust
nodes.norm_label: decision 037: workspace cache aliases, extension pins, and trust

nodes.label: permwrapper -> wrapper Gradle distribution alias
nodes.rationale: Bundled robot-starter primes GRADLE_USER_HOME using distributionPath=wrapper/dists, but WPILib-generated projects use permwrapper/dists; since Gradle derives the extraction directory name from distributionUrl not distributionPath, a relative symlink alias lets both layouts share one cached extraction, avoiding a redundant ~146 MiB download per imported team project.

nodes.label: --do-not-include-pack-dependencies flag
nodes.rationale: codium-server --install-extension normally resolves extensionPack/extensionDependencies via Open VSX, silently replacing four pinned VSIX versions with gallery-latest builds and making the image build time-dependent; the flag disables that, with an exact extensions.json manifest assertion catching future drift.

nodes.label: --disable-workspace-trust server flag
nodes.rationale: Server-side settings cannot disable the application-scoped workspace-trust setting; the server exposes a CLI flag that passes enableWorkspaceTrust:false to the workbench directly, no patch needed. Tradeoff: removes VS Code's protection against repository-controlled automatic behavior for a classroom flow needing immediate Java support; container isolation remains the security boundary between students and host.

nodes.label: Gradle daemon JVM args rejected by Tooling API
nodes.rationale: vscjava.vscode-gradle forwarded java.import.gradle.jvmArguments to BuildLauncher.setJvmArguments(), which rejects -Xms/-Xmx/-XX tokens as unknown command-line options, producing a persistent Gradle error status beside Java:Ready; removed since the same limits already live in gradle.properties org.gradle.jvmargs, which command-line builds read.
nodes.norm_label: gradle daemon jvm args rejected by tooling api

nodes.label: Decision 038: Java tooling compatibility, extension reconciliation, and real-image smoke
nodes.norm_label: decision 038: java tooling compatibility, extension reconciliation, and real-image smoke

nodes.label: Separate tooling (JDT, Java 21) and project (Java 17) JDKs
nodes.rationale: Enforcing pinned VSIX versions (no gallery resolution) exposed that Java Debug 0.59 and current JDT bundles require JavaSE 21 while the image only supplied Temurin 17. WPILib extension 2026.1.1 reads java.jdt.ls.java.home first and forces it onto every Gradle task as JAVA_HOME, breaking the robot's Spotless step on Java21; corrected split leaves java.jdt.ls.java.home unset, supplies Java21 via JDK_HOME (which Red Hat Java discovers), and keeps JAVA_HOME on Java17 (which WPILib falls through to).
nodes.norm_label: separate tooling (jdt, java 21) and project (java 17) jdks

nodes.label: Managed extension reconciliation on every container start
nodes.rationale: First-boot-only copying left existing /config/extensions homes permanently on old pins; init-frc-setup now reconciles only the nine CodeRunner-managed IDs against the baked manifest, removing/replacing only managed directories while preserving student-installed extensions.
nodes.norm_label: managed extension reconciliation on every container start

nodes.label: bun run e2e:workspace-java real-container smoke
nodes.rationale: A manifest/version assertion could not detect the incompatible extension-JDK bundle matrix (No delegateCommandHandler for vscode.java.resolveMainMethod); a real Playwright-driven container smoke is required acceptance for any workspace JDK/editor-base/Java extension/init change.

nodes.label: Deploy-files API (/u/:slug/api/deploy-files/...)
nodes.rationale: Additive API behind requireWorkspaceOwnership hydrating an in-memory PathPlanner GUI copy over HTTP: read-write for src/main/deploy/pathplanner/**, read-only for choreo/**, path-validated by a shared contracts schema, 5MB file cap, no rename op (client decomposes to PUT+DELETE).

nodes.label: pathplanner-dist.tar.gz packaging
nodes.rationale: A prebuilt tarball is fetched from the fork's GitHub releases and baked into the control image by a dedicated Dockerfile stage so Flutter never enters this repo's toolchain; required for release build paths, optional for demo/recovery paths where /pathplanner/ serves a 503 if skipped.

nodes.label: Single-stage Dockerfile with baked Gradle cache
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage builds shrink images by discarding tooling, but here ~/.gradle/caches must be baked into the final image so container startup doesn't re-download WPILib jars/natives every run; copying caches between stages defeats that, so single stage is accepted at ~1GB (later measured 2.25GB).
nodes.norm_label: single-stage dockerfile with baked gradle cache

nodes.label: Headless sim via omission, not flag
nodes.rationale: GradleRIO 2026 opts SimGUI and DriverStation sim in via wpi.sim.addGui()/addDriverstation() in build.gradle, both enabled by the stock template; simply deleting those two lines yields a pure-JVM NT4Server-only sim with no X server/DISPLAY needed, avoiding a -PsimExtensions flag hack.
nodes.norm_label: headless sim via omission, not flag

nodes.label: eclipse-temurin:17-jdk-jammy base image choice
nodes.rationale: WPILib 2026 targets JDK17 so JRE-only would break Gradle annotation processing; Alpine is musl-based and WPILib native libs are glibc-built; gradle:8-jdk17's bundled Gradle would be ignored since the wrapper pins the version; jammy chosen over noble for slightly smaller image.

nodes.label: StructPublisher<Pose2d> telemetry choice
nodes.rationale: AdvantageScope auto-decodes Pose2d struct topics for the 2D Field tab; a raw double[3] array would work but lose the type info AS uses for visualization defaults.

nodes.label: AS Lite window.location.hostname NT4 auto-detection
nodes.rationale: When built with ASCOPE_DISTRIBUTION=LITE, hub.ts picks window.location.hostname as the live NT4 data source address and NT4_PORTS_DEFAULT[0]=5810 is hardcoded, so serving Lite from the same host as the sim's NT4 server works with zero source modifications, query params, or postMessage shims — and the same property makes iframe embedding cross-origin-free later.

nodes.label: AS Lite GET /assets and /assets/<name>/<file> routes
nodes.rationale: Without these two routes mirroring upstream lite_server.py, the page loads but the field/robot 3D model pickers are empty (404 /assets); a Fastify server registers both ahead of @fastify/static, caching a manifest of bundledAssets/ built at startup.

nodes.label: AdvantageScope git submodule pinned to release tag
nodes.rationale: Pinning to a stable tag (v26.0.2) rather than tracking main keeps builds reproducible, since upstream could rename the build script or change a depended-on flag at any time.
nodes.norm_label: advantagescope git submodule pinned to release tag

nodes.label: Vanilla TypeScript + Vite web shell (no framework)
nodes.rationale: The MVP spec explicitly allows vanilla TS+Vite and warns the frontend will likely be rewritten post-MVP, so React/Vue/Svelte would add a build-graph node and learning surface for zero benefit at this scale ('boring obvious option').
nodes.norm_label: vanilla typescript + vite web shell (no framework)

nodes.label: AS Lite embedded via iframe, not bundled/proxied
nodes.rationale: An iframe from http://localhost:8080 sees window.location.hostname===localhost regardless of the parent frame's origin, giving zero cross-origin config and sandboxing WebGL/wasm; rejected alternatives were a Vite proxy (would need rewriting the /assets manifest route) and bundling dist/advantagescope into the web app (couples build pipelines, bloats dev-server cold start).
nodes.norm_label: as lite embedded via iframe, not bundled/proxied

nodes.label: CSS grid layout: AS Lite spans full right column
nodes.rationale: First-cut layout let the console row span full width, clipping AS Lite's 200px tab-controls panel positioned relative to its own (shrunk) viewport bottom; giving AS Lite the full right-column height fixed the clipping and is also more semantic (console=editor concern, AS Lite=sim concern).
nodes.norm_label: css grid layout: as lite spans full right column

nodes.label: Archive 004: Backend wiring for save and run
nodes.norm_label: archive 004: backend wiring for save and run

nodes.label: Host backend plus Docker CLI (fixed argument arrays)
nodes.rationale: Matches MVP scope of one named container/one file path/no dynamic scheduling; avoids adding dockerode or broader orchestration dependency for a single-user MVP.
nodes.norm_label: host backend plus docker cli (fixed argument arrays)

nodes.label: Custom WebSocket sender (no @fastify/websocket)
nodes.rationale: @fastify/websocket was unavailable (no npm on PATH); since /run is server-to-client text streaming only, the backend implements the handshake and unmasked text frames directly on Node's HTTP upgrade event, deliberately narrow — to be replaced if the protocol grows.

nodes.label: Replaceable sim process under tini
nodes.rationale: start-sim.sh/stop-sim.sh let Run stop and restart the sim without replacing the container; entrypoint runs under tini because a backgrounded Gradle/Java process could become an orphan zombie under PID1 without an init/reaper, causing every rebuild to wait for the 10-second hard-kill path.

nodes.label: Plain Monaco client with direct LSP requests
nodes.rationale: TypeFox's MonacoVscodeApiWrapper/EditorApp/LanguageClientWrapper connected but was unreliable driving live-buffer diagnostics/completions; a small direct LSP adapter (java-lsp.ts) sending initialize/didOpen/didChange and registering Monaco hover/completion/diagnostics providers proved more reliable.
nodes.norm_label: plain monaco client with direct lsp requests

nodes.label: Per-student sim + JDT LS containers, path-routed sessions
nodes.rationale: A shared-process JDT LS test showed diagnostics working for one workspace folder but missing notifications for a second broken buffer, and would need a browser-session broker to safely multiplex Monaco clients — more work/risk than the memory saved for ~10 students. Recommendation: per-student containers, URL-path session identity (/u/<session>/...) at the edge rather than query params, and a WS proxy demuxing NT4 by path with a small AS Lite source-level patch for endpoint injection.
nodes.norm_label: per-student sim + jdt ls containers, path-routed sessions

nodes.label: NT4 WS proxy demuxing by path (apps/router)
nodes.norm_label: nt4 ws proxy demuxing by path (apps/router)

nodes.label: Docker labels as runtime source of truth, SQLite as cache
nodes.rationale: frc-sim.managed/version/role/workspace labels let the orchestrator find managed containers after a control-plane restart and re-sync SQLite from Docker's published port/runtime state; SQLite remains useful history/cache but Docker is authoritative.
nodes.norm_label: docker labels as runtime source of truth, sqlite as cache

nodes.label: Loopback-only published NT4 ports
nodes.rationale: Sim NT4 published only as 127.0.0.1:<port>:5810; reconciliation removes and recreates any managed container found published on a non-loopback host address, forcing browser routes through control-plane paths instead of the raw port.

nodes.label: Runtime Gradle cache seed from /opt/frc-gradle-cache
nodes.rationale: An empty mounted /home/frc workspace home would hide the Gradle cache baked at image-build time; the entrypoint seeds a fresh mounted GRADLE_USER_HOME from a preserved /opt/frc-gradle-cache copy at container start, preserving warm startup under the mounted-home contract.

nodes.label: Decision 013: per-workspace NT4 isolation
nodes.rationale: Each workspace's NT4 traffic must remain isolated; cross-workspace NT4 proxy access is rejected with 403.

nodes.label: deny-list rationale for PathPlanner deploy file paths
nodes.rationale: PathPlanner lets students name paths/autos freely with punctuation and non-ASCII characters, so a deny-list of unsafe characters is used instead of an allow-list, while still guarding against path traversal via segments starting with '.'.
nodes.norm_label: deny-list rationale for pathplanner deploy file paths

nodes.label: P9 JSON round-trip property
nodes.rationale: Any object that passes schema.parse() should re-pass validation after JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)), catching schemas that allow non-JSON values like Date, undefined, or functions.

nodes.label: P10 reject-malformed-input property
nodes.rationale: Every schema (slug regex, axis bounds, etc.) must reject malformed inputs.

nodes.label: embedded-mode NT4 endpoint injection mechanism
nodes.rationale: /scope/?frcEndpoint=postMessage waits for the parent page to send frc-sim:set-nt4-endpoint, acknowledges with frc-sim:nt4-endpoint-ready, and starts the live NT4 connection using the injected endpoint, so the AS Lite iframe can be pointed at a per-workspace NT4 proxy without hardcoding the URL.

nodes.label: data/users/<workspaceId>/{project,assets} backup layout
nodes.rationale: Backs up app.db, allowlist.json, and per-workspace project/assets as tarballs; excludes regenerable per-workspace data (home/, jdtls-data/, logs/) since only student data and config need preserving.

nodes.label: skip owlet/docs postinstall rationale
nodes.rationale: Upstream postinstall downloads ~7 platform binaries for desktop OCR/AprilTag tooling not needed for AS Lite, and builds an unused docs workspace, so only the steps Lite's compile and asset staging depend on are run.
